project.title: Killer In The Keep
project.subtitle: An Among Us + Clue + D&D Social-Deduction Dungeon Video Game
project.high_concept: Two to eight human players enter a storm-bound, monster-infested keep. Every match secretly assigns exactly one active adventurer—human or bot—as the main killer and seals that same character together with one murder weapon and one murder room in the authoritative evidence envelope. The killer is privately told their role at match start. All players roll to move across a fully clickable board, investigate rooms, report bodies, debate suspicions, use secret passages, fight D&D-style monsters and rivals, disarm or exploit traps, collect and use treasure, and attempt a final three-part accusation. The two modes are cooperative investigators versus the hidden killer, or full PvP where anyone may attack while only the sealed character is the main killer.

supported_players.bot_fill_rule: When human_players < 6, add 6 - human_players adventurer bots.
supported_players.unique_hero_rule: Every human or adventurer bot controls one unique hero; no hero may be duplicated in the same match.

project.playstyle_statement: Both modes use the same clickable keep board, roll-to-move system, mandatory hidden killer, sealed suspect/weapon/room envelope, reports and discussion, secret passages, monsters, traps, treasure, inventory, D&D combat, bots, and ending reconstruction. Work Together disables innocent-on-innocent damage and treats the non-killers as one investigation team; Full PvP permits every adventurer to fight, steal, bluff, betray, and pursue an individual victory, making the main killer harder to identify because ordinary PvP violence does not prove who committed the original murder.

controller_compatibility: Xbox Series S/X, Xbox One, and Xbox 360-compatible controllers
PlayStation 2 and later compatible controller layouts
platform_and_input_scope.touch_controls: May mirror the same context actions through an on-screen control layout.

among_us_style: Exactly one privately informed main killer in every match
Timed discussions, suspicion pings, and optional detention votes

Human or bot may receive the killer role

Private evidence cards and ordered disproval

Distinct heroes, powers, weapons, armor, and advancement
Usable, equippable, tradeable, droppable, and lootable treasure and items

opening_story.setup: Eight travelers seek refuge from a violent storm. A painful cry comes from deep inside the keep. The master is found dead, blood stains the floor, the exits become unsafe or magically sealed, and evidence indicates that one of the eight adventurers committed the murder.
central_questions: Which character killed the master of the keep?
In which room did the murder occur?

playstyles.description: All non-killer heroes are one investigation party. Exactly one active hero is secretly the killer. Innocents share survival and deduction goals, cannot intentionally damage one another, and must expose the killer, weapon, and room while surviving monsters, traps, sabotage, and hidden attacks.
playstyles.player_versus_player: killer-versus-investigators only; non-killer friendly fire is blocked

information_model.private_evidence: Evidence cards remain private until voluntarily shared or revealed by a rule.
information_model.sharing: Non-killers may reveal evidence, ping clues, use voice/text discussion, and build one shared case board.
information_model.shared_notebook: Publicly revealed exclusions, witnessed attacks, sabotage evidence, and confirmed timelines are recorded for the team.
information_model.killer_deception: The killer may lie, withhold, frame, plant non-card clues, and sabotage, but cannot forge server-verified evidence cards or dice.

cooperation_features: Shared movement and route planning after each roll
Assisted searches, lockpicking, trap disarming, rescues, healing, and revivals
Team vote on a proposed final accusation
playstyles.death_rule: At confirmed death, the player enters Ghost Mode. The ghost may see every player and move through walls and between floors, but cannot report, call meetings, vote, accuse, communicate clues to living players, interact with gameplay, or affect the match. A legal revival within two rounds returns the player to living play.
victory_conditions: A surviving eligible non-killer makes the correct suspect, weapon, and room accusation.
Optional proof-and-capture rule: the killer is physically defeated or restrained and the team correctly proves the weapon and room.
defeat_conditions: The killer eliminates or permanently incapacitates enough investigators that no eligible accuser remains.
The killer completes the configured escape, ritual, or storm sabotage objective.
Every non-killer is dead or permanently incapacitated.
The team makes an incorrect strict final accusation.
playstyles.bot_fill: If fewer than six humans join, adventurer bots fill unique hero slots until the match has six adventurers.
playstyles.bot_role: Non-killer bots cooperate; the single killer bot secretly deceives, sabotages, stalks, and attacks under the killer AI profile.
playstyles.human_and_bot_victory: All surviving non-killers share victory. The killer has a separate opposing victory condition.
playstyles.killer_visibility: Private to the killer until witnessed, exposed by powers, or revealed at match end.

start_placement.rule: All active adventurer tokens begin in unique Foyer cells arranged in two rows.

playstyles.description: Every hero is an independent rival and all legal PvP is enabled. Exactly one active hero is still the secretly assigned main killer in the sealed envelope. Any player may attack, rob, betray, revive, or kill another player, so violence alone does not identify the original murderer.

information_model.private_evidence: Each player and bot has a private hand, private notebook, and private objective history.
information_model.sharing: Information is shared only through voluntary reveals, bargains, threats, theft rules, witnessed events, meetings, or abilities.
information_model.deception: All players may bluff. The main killer additionally receives sabotage and framing actions. No one may falsify server-verified dice, cards, item instances, or movement.

alliance_rules: Temporary alliances may form, dissolve, or be betrayed at any time.
Alliance members remain independently eligible to win.
Players may attack, down, revive, rob, trade with, or abandon rivals as allowed by action economy.
Killing an innocent does not reveal or transfer the main-killer role.
A witnessed attack is logged as violence evidence, not proof of the original murder.
playstyles.death_rule: At confirmed death, the player enters Ghost Mode. The ghost may see every player and move through walls and between floors, but cannot report, call meetings, vote, accuse, communicate clues to living players, interact with gameplay, or affect the match. A legal revival within two rounds returns the player to living play.
victory_conditions: A non-killer is the first eligible player to make the correct suspect, weapon, and room accusation.
The main killer wins by completing the killer escape/sabotage condition or eliminating all eligible rivals before a correct accusation.
Optional elimination victory may rank the last living independent hero, but it never changes who the sealed main killer was.
playstyles.tie_breaker: If the mystery ends without a unique primary winner, recovered treasure value determines placement.
special_character_rules: After Keep Rank 2, Gunnus may raise an eliminated hero as a zombie under his control.
Under the legacy false-accusation duel rule, Jock may teleport to a player who falsely implicates Jock and take the first combat turn.
A player who defeats another hero receives the defeated hero's unspent run XP in Legacy Rules mode.

scoring.primary: Solve the murder first or remain the last living independent hero.

playstyles.bot_fill: If fewer than six humans join, adventurer bots fill unique hero slots until the match has six adventurers.
playstyles.bot_role: All bots are independent rivals; the secretly selected killer bot also uses killer-only sabotage and deception logic.
playstyles.human_and_bot_victory: Each adventurer has an independent placement. The main killer follows killer victory rules and cannot win by submitting the known solution as an investigator.
playstyles.main_killer_distinction: Only the sealed suspect is the main killer. Other players may commit PvP attacks or kills without becoming the main killer or changing the envelope.

start_placement.rule: Each of the eight characters begins in a different approved room across all four floors. The Armory is forbidden as a start room.

run_setup: Select Work Together: Find the Killer or Full PvP.
Choose difficulty, movement-roll profile, D&D combat profile, accusation consequences, meeting rules, and accessibility options.
Create a lobby for two to eight human players.
If fewer than six humans are present, add enough unique adventurer bots to reach six total adventurers.
Assign one unique hero to every human and adventurer bot.
Each hero chooses two unlimited powers and one starting limited power.
The authoritative server chooses exactly one active hero as the main killer and stores that hero as the suspect card in the sealed envelope.
The authoritative server also chooses one murder weapon and one murder room, completing the three-card envelope.
The killer alone receives a private role reveal and private murder memory; every non-killer receives a private innocent role reveal.
All remaining suspect, weapon, and room cards are dealt privately as evenly as possible.
Spawn monsters, traps, treasure, searchable containers, objective stations, secret passages, and clue instances from the match seed.
Place each hero token at its color-coded starting square and begin the first exploration movement roll.
core_loop: Calculate and highlight every legal end square reachable by that roll.
Select a highlighted destination and animate the token along the authoritative legal path.
Resolve the destination square, room entry, secret passage, clue, body, monster, trap, treasure, objective, or player encounter.
Use D&D-style actions, attacks, powers, checks, saving throws, conditions, healing, and initiative when an encounter begins.
Report bodies or major incidents, discuss suspicions, and record public or private evidence.
Search rooms, use items, trade or steal where permitted, gain XP, and unlock Game Levels.
Make room theories to obtain exclusions and continue deducing the sealed suspect, weapon, and room.
The killer secretly sabotages, frames, stalks, attacks, or works toward escape while avoiding exposure.
An eligible non-killer commits to a final accusation, or the killer completes a killer victory condition.

solution_generation.authority: The authoritative server creates, encrypts, and stores the full envelope. The full solution is sent only to the authenticated killer session as a private role payload and is never included in public match state, ordinary bot context, replay snapshots visible during the match, or non-killer clients.
solution_generation.player_character_rule: The selected culprit must be one active human-controlled or bot-controlled hero. That controller is privately told at match start that they are the main killer. The sealed suspect ID exactly equals the killer role holder ID for the entire match.
killer_knows: their private killer objectives and cooldowns
non_killers_know: the public rules and player roster
only evidence legitimately dealt, found, witnessed, or shared
solution_generation.immutability: The envelope cannot change after the first player receives a role payload. Disconnects use role-preserving reconnect; bot takeover inherits the same role without rerolling.
solution_generation.killer_accusation_restriction: Because the killer knows the envelope, the killer cannot win through an investigator final accusation and cannot submit the true solution as a scoring accusation.

recommended_profile.name: D&D Adventure Rules
recommended_profile.description: Uses familiar D&D-style tactical combat and skill resolution while preserving the board game's unique murder, card, rank, treasure, trap, and elimination systems.
turn_structure: One reaction before the character's next turn
Free interaction with one nearby object
recommended_profile.initiative: Roll d20 plus Dexterity or use a simultaneous planning option in Work Together.

resting.short_rest: A defended pause that restores selected class resources and allows limited healing.
resting.long_rest: A risky multi-turn rest that refreshes limited powers but can advance the storm, spawn patrols, or allow rivals to move.

recommended_profile.death: At 0 HP, a hero is Downed and uses death-saving throws. Confirmed death begins Ghost Mode; a legal restoration within two rounds ends Ghost Mode and returns the hero to living play.
recommended_profile.balance_note: Final hit points, armor class, spell damage, save DCs, and monster statistics should be normalized to one selected D&D SRD rules baseline during production.

legacy_profile.name: Legacy Board Rules
legacy_profile.description: Preserves the original board-game math and pacing as a selectable digital rules mode.
legacy_profile.initiative: All players roll 1d10; the highest result acts first, followed by lobby order.
legacy_profile.movement: Roll 1d10 and move that many 5-foot spaces.
level_up_triggers: Correctly identify two previously unknown solution cards.
legacy_profile.future_xp_formula: Each later threshold equals the previous threshold multiplied by 3.
legacy_profile.power_uses: A limited power has one use at starting rank, two uses at Rank 1, three uses at Rank 2, and so on.
legacy_profile.legacy_long_rest: Skip three turns to refresh limited powers.
legacy_profile.legacy_lockpick: Roll 1d10; 7 or higher succeeds, while a natural 1 destroys or forfeits the lockpick.

keep_rank_system.purpose: Fast progression within a single mystery without requiring the heroes to gain many normal D&D levels.
on_rank_up: Restore the hero to full health in Legacy mode.
Increase maximum health by 5 in Legacy mode.
Unlock a new power from the current or an earlier rank.
Unlock class-specific armor or resource improvements.

free/object interactions as allowed by DM

Understand puzzles, locks, false tasks, clues, safe routes, and mechanisms.

exploration_actions.roll: Usually spell effect; Arcana may identify details
exploration_actions.use: Locate magical auras, glyphs, wards, curses, illusions, and spell traps.

exploration_actions.use: Disable traps, locks, runes, pressure plates, conduits, and alarms.

Give an ally advantage when your character can meaningfully assist.

what_wins_the_game: Rescue protected NPCs or recover key items
what_loses_the_game: All player characters are down, dead, captured, or unable to act
The party chooses retreat and abandons the mission

quick_formula_reference.saving_throw: 1d20 + ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient in that save
quick_formula_reference.weapon_attack: 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient with the weapon
quick_formula_reference.weapon_damage: weapon damage dice + relevant ability modifier unless a rule says otherwise

start_combat_when: hostile and player become mutually aware
initiative_turn_attack_engine.turn_order: Sort descending; ties resolved by player choice for PCs and bot/tie rule for hostiles.
combat_turn_resources: one reaction between turns when triggered
free/object interactions as allowed by DM

On a hit, roll damage and apply effects.

attack_formulas.weapon_attack: 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + proficiency bonus if proficient with the weapon
attack_formulas.weapon_damage: weapon damage dice + relevant ability modifier unless a rule says otherwise

bot_initiative_modes.grouped_by_type: All identical minions share one initiative result.
bot_initiative_modes.lair_plus_minions: Boss, lair, and minions each get separate initiative slots.
bot_initiative_modes.fast_mobile_game: Players share one block and hostiles share one block, useful for quick sessions.

downed_rules.default: At 0 HP a PC follows the table's death save/downed rules, not an Among Us instant-kill model.
downed_rules.mini_game_safe_mode: At 0 HP, a PC is knocked out/captured until stabilized or the encounter ends.
downed_rules.hardcore_mode: Use normal death saves and consequences.

detection_perception_magic_rules.passive_perception: 10 + Wisdom (Perception) modifiers; used for hidden traps/hostiles when players are not actively searching.
detection_perception_magic_rules.active_perception: Wisdom (Perception) when looking, listening, smelling, watching shadows, or scanning a room.
detection_perception_magic_rules.investigation: Intelligence (Investigation) when deducing how something works, finding mechanisms, reading patterns, or checking a specific object.
detection_perception_magic_rules.detect_magic: Reveals the presence of magic/aura where the spell or mini-game setting allows; Arcana may identify the school, trigger, anchor, or disarm method.

degrees_of_success.fail_by_10_or_more: false confidence or trap triggers if interacted with
degrees_of_success.fail: not found yet; time may pass
degrees_of_success.success_by_5_or_more: threat located plus disarm clue, safe route, or bot behavior hint
degrees_of_success.natural_20_optional: extra clue, advantage to next ally, or safe shortcut

rules_basis.preferred: Revised fifth-edition/SRD-compatible d20 engine configured consistently.
rules_basis.legacy_option: Existing Killer In The Keep Legacy Board profile remains selectable.

attached_unified_runtime.core_formula: Roll 1d20 + relevant ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus when proficient + other explicit modifiers; compare with Armor Class or Difficulty Class.
turn_resources: one Bonus Action only when granted
one Reaction before the next turn when triggered

flow.localized_initiative: Monster, hostile Trap, or PvP threats place involved characters into initiative.
flow.legacy_board_movement: Optional movement-roll profile may highlight reachable squares and move the selected token to the chosen legal endpoint.

death.opening_exception: The off-screen first-victim cinematic may bypass ordinary combat.

work_together_default.at_zero_hp: Downed and incapacitated with a two-round rescue window.
work_together_default.permanent_death: If not stabilized, healed, or restored before the rescue window closes, return cards and enter Ghost Mode.
work_together_default.hardcore_option: The host may enable the Free For All death-save procedure.

free_for_all.at_zero_hp: Unconscious/downed and begin Death Saving Throws.
free_for_all.roll_timing: Roll 1d20 at the start of the downed character’s turn.
free_for_all.success: 10 or higher; three successes makes the character Stable.
free_for_all.failure: 9 or lower; three failures causes permanent death.
free_for_all.natural_20: Regain 1 HP immediately and end the downed state.
free_for_all.damage_at_zero: Applies death-save failures and may cause instant death according to the selected D&D profile.
free_for_all.bot_rule: Character bots roll and resolve the same server-visible death saves as human characters.
free_for_all.permanent_death: Return all deck-owned cards, shuffle affected decks, and enter Ghost Mode.

death.zero_hp: Use the configured unconscious/downed and death-saving-throw rules.
death.permanent_death: Return cards atomically and enter ghost mode.

attached_unified_runtime.monster_encounter: Monster cards pop up, spawn fightable monsters, and use initiative, AC, HP, attacks, saving throws, conditions, and legal AI.
attached_unified_runtime.trap_encounter: Random Trap cards use real-time or round-based countdowns plus checks, tools, spells, saves, movement, and environmental counterplay.
attached_unified_runtime.treasure: Treasure cards create usable inventory and risk/reward decisions.

terminology.game_level: The only level number shown for in-session progression. Valid values are 1 through 5.
terminology.dnd_equivalent_level: The D&D power snapshot represented by that Game Level. It is not an additional progression track.
terminology.keep_rank: Deprecated term. Do not display or use it for canonical gameplay.

five_game_levels.clarification: Five Game Levels means five total level states in a session. Players start at Game Level 1 and can level up four times, ending at Game Level 5. It does not mean five additional level-ups after the starting level.

level_table.ability_jump: Begin with the complete curated D&D level 5-equivalent hero package, including the hero's unlimited powers, starting limited powers, starting equipment, and level-appropriate combat statistics.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 9-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 2. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.
Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 13-equivalent package and unlock the abilities assigned to Game Level 3. Intermediate D&D level choices are not processed separately.

Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 17-equivalent package. This is a major high-tier class-feature, armor, resource, spell, save DC, and combat-stat jump even when no new named power is listed.

level_table.session_role: Fourth and final level-up / session maximum
level_table.ability_jump: Immediately replace or upgrade the hero to the curated D&D level 20-equivalent package, unlock the final named powers, and apply the hero's session capstone. No progression beyond Game Level 5 is permitted during the session.

ability_jump_policy.snapshot_rule: Each Game Level is a curated destination package. On level-up, the character sheet immediately applies the destination D&D-equivalent statistics, class features, spell access, resource limits, armor improvements, and assigned powers.
ability_jump_policy.no_intermediate_processing: Do not make the player process each skipped D&D level one at a time. Only choices explicitly included in the destination package receive prompts.
ability_jump_policy.power_unlock_rule: Named powers are assigned by Game Level. Existing powers may also receive damage, range, duration, target-count, save DC, resource, or use-count upgrades at every Game Level.
ability_jump_policy.maximum_rule: When Game Level 5 is reached, further XP or level-up triggers cannot increase the character level during that session.

on_level_up: Advance exactly one Game Level, never more than one level from a single resolved trigger.
Apply the destination D&D-equivalent character package immediately.
Restore the hero to full health in Legacy mode.
Increase maximum health by 5 in Legacy mode.
Increase limited-power uses to equal the new Game Level unless a specific power states otherwise.
Unlock the named powers and class-specific upgrades assigned to the new Game Level.
Apply any armor, spell, proficiency, save DC, resource, or capstone upgrades assigned to the destination package.
Stop all further in-session leveling after Game Level 5.

valid_triggers: Roll a natural 20 during combat when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach the cumulative XP threshold for the next Game Level.
Correctly identify two previously unknown solution cards when Legacy Rules allow this trigger.
Reach a configured story milestone or objective checkpoint.
trigger_resolution.same_event_limit: A single event can grant at most one Game Level even if it satisfies multiple triggers.
trigger_resolution.maximum_level_guard: Ignore or convert additional level-up triggers into non-level rewards after Game Level 5.

health_bars.players_and_character_bots: Every living player character and character bot has a current/max HP bar in the party/roster HUD and above the token when targeted or damaged.
health_bars.monsters: Every revealed monster has a current/max HP bar. Bosses may use phase segments but still retain authoritative HP.
health_bars.ghosts: Ghosts have Haunt Energy rather than living HP and cannot be reduced by ordinary weapon damage.
health_bars.server_authority: All damage, healing, temporary HP, maximum HP, death-save state, and monster HP are server-authoritative.

search_locks_and_traps.search_action: Use an action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check against the fixture’s notice/detection DC to find a concealed trap, lock detail, hidden chest, secret latch, or concealed object.
search_locks_and_traps.passive_perception: Passive Perception can provide a warning that something is wrong, but this game still requires the active Perception roll before safely manipulating a chest, bookshelf, trapped door, or secret passage.
search_locks_and_traps.authored_trap_card: If a fixture has trap_ref/card_ref, reveal that exact Trap card after detection or triggering. Otherwise draw the top random Trap card when the fixture is marked trapped.
search_locks_and_traps.disarm_action: Use a Utilize action and make a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the authored disable DC; default DC 15 when no DC is supplied.
search_locks_and_traps.lockpick_action: Picking a lock is separate from disarming its trap: make a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the authored lock DC; default DC 15 when none is supplied.
order_for_locked_and_trapped_fixture: Pick, force, magically open, or bypass lock
search_locks_and_traps.help: A nearby proficient ally can take the Help action to grant Advantage on the next applicable skill or tool check.
search_locks_and_traps.crowbar: A crowbar grants Advantage on Strength checks where leverage applies.
search_locks_and_traps.brute_force_house_rule: Without Thieves’ Tools, a character may attempt Strength (Athletics) against lock DC + 3. The attempt is noisy, cannot delicately disarm the trap, may damage contents, and may activate a monster trigger.
search_locks_and_traps.failure: A failed disarm normally triggers the trap. A failed lockpick jams or alarms the fixture only when its card or authored data says so.

fixture_investigation.chests: Every chest uses Search → trap resolution → lock resolution → Treasure draw/reveal. Authored contents are revealed as their listed Treasure cards; an unspecified chest draws the top Treasure card.

bookshelves.sequence: Search for traps or hidden mechanisms. On a trapped result, resolve a Trap card; on a monster-ambush result, draw and spawn from the Monster deck. After safe resolution, draw from the Treasure deck or reveal the authored room reward.
bookshelves.library_spider: The attached Library bookshelf search can activate the authored hidden spider at L13.

fixture_investigation.weapon_racks: Search/investigate the rack, resolve its monster or trap trigger, then draw one Armory Weapon card.

health_bars.players_and_bots: Always show current HP and maximum HP to the owning player; show teammates/opponents according to mode visibility settings.
health_bars.bloodied_marker: Display Bloodied at half maximum HP or fewer.
health_bars.monsters: All monster entities store current/max HP and display an HP bar once discovered.

free_for_all_death_saves.start_of_turn: Roll 1d20: 10+ is a success; 9 or less is a failure.
free_for_all_death_saves.three_failures: Permanent death, card return, then Ghost Mode.
free_for_all_death_saves.damage_at_zero: One failure; a critical hit causes two; damage at least equal to maximum HP causes death.
free_for_all_death_saves.stabilize: A living helper can use an action and succeed on DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine); a Healer’s Kit can stabilize according to its item rules.

hp_death_and_ghost_transition.work_together_default: Uses the same downed and death-saving procedure unless a host explicitly chooses the easier rescue profile.
hp_death_and_ghost_transition.opening_victim_exception: The opening victim is already permanently dead at setup and makes no death saves.
hp_death_and_ghost_transition.revival: If a legal revival restores life, evidence and Treasure cards already returned remain in circulation; do not recreate duplicates.

magic_item_runtime.inventory_ui: Show equipped, carried, stowed, consumable, attuned, charges, and recharge timing.
magic_item_runtime.typed_damage: Display base physical damage and extra Acid/Cold/Fire/Force/Lightning/Necrotic/Poison/Psychic/Radiant/Thunder damage separately.
magic_item_runtime.saving_throws: Resolve item saving throws server-authoritatively using the DC on the card.
magic_item_runtime.edition: Use SRD 5.2.1 action names; a 2014 compatibility mode can map Magic/Utilize actions to the nearest 2014 action without changing card ownership.

evidence_layers.purpose: Blood patterns, footprints, magical residue, poison traces, broken objects, fibers, weapon marks, and room disturbances.
Statements from surviving servants, spectral echoes, familiars, animated objects, and other heroes.
Establish where characters could or could not have been when the murder occurred.
Arcana, Religion, Nature, Medicine, and martial knowledge reveal different interpretations.

room_theory.availability: A player standing in a solution room may propose one suspect, one weapon, and that room.
room_theory.legacy_check: A DC 13 Wisdom check is required before making the theory.
room_theory.response: The first eligible player in turn order who holds a matching card privately reveals one matching card to the theorist.
room_theory.digital_notebook: The revealed card is automatically marked only in the receiving player's notebook unless it is publicly shared.
room_theory.owned_room_exception: Once per visit, a player holding the current room card may publicly discard it and propose a different room under the original special rule.

final_accusation.presentation: The accused character, weapon, and room are selected on a three-part case board.
final_accusation.resolution: Lock the request atomically, compare all three categories to the sealed envelope, then begin the Final Confrontation on a correct result.
incorrect_accusation_options: Strict: the accuser can no longer win by deduction.
Standard: the accuser receives a major penalty and must discover new evidence before trying again.
Casual: the accusation simply fails and the run continues.
final_accusation.room_validation: The submitted room must equal the room currently occupied by the accuser. Either Library floor counts as the Library.
eligibility: has not used strict final accusation
holds none of the three submitted cards
exact combination was not disproved in the immediately preceding Room Accusation
final_accusation.work_together: The team confirms a shared Final Accusation from the physical room. A wrong strict accusation grants the original killer victory unless forgiving mode is enabled.
final_accusation.free_for_all: Each eligible living non-killer gets one strict Final Accusation. A wrong accuser follows the configured lethal consequence, returns all cards, and becomes a ghost without learning which field was wrong.
final_accusation.correct: Reveal the opening murder reconstruction, the original killer, weapon, victim, and room, then begin the configured Final Confrontation/capture/escape sequence.
final_accusation.killer_restriction: The original killer knows the solution but can never submit it as a winning accusation.
requirements: holds none of the three accused cards
no active meeting or unresolved forced encounter
final_accusation.wrong_work_together: Apply the configured strict-team failure or remove that accuser’s future accusation eligibility.
final_accusation.wrong_free_for_all: The accuser permanently dies, returns all deck-owned cards, and immediately becomes a ghost.

logical_inference_patterns.name: Single-card isolation
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: Suggest two cards from your own hand plus one unknown card. Any opponent who disproves must be showing the unknown card, because the two controlled cards cannot be in an opponent's hand.

logical_inference_patterns.name: Pass-chain elimination
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: For each player who passes before a card is shown, eliminate all three suggested cards from that player's hand.

logical_inference_patterns.name: Resolved disjunction
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: If a player previously showed one of A/B/C and later A and B are proven to belong elsewhere, that player must hold C.

logical_inference_patterns.name: Category completion
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: When five of six suspects are known outside the envelope, the sixth suspect must be the solution suspect. Equivalent logic applies to weapons and rooms.

logical_inference_patterns.name: Hand-capacity reasoning
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: If all cards in a player's hand have been identified, every other card can be eliminated from that player's possible holdings.

logical_inference_patterns.name: No-answer inference
logical_inference_patterns.pattern: If every opponent passes and the active player does not hold a named card, that card must be in the envelope unless the edition has public, face-down, or set-aside cards outside all hands.

privacy_requirements: Never expose the solution to a client before a valid accusation check.
Send a private reveal only to the suggesting player's authenticated session.

Keep private notes client-scoped unless team rules explicitly share them.
Log deterministic rule events for dispute resolution without leaking hidden data to players.

suggestion_resolution_algorithm: Validate that the active token is in a room.
Validate that the named room equals the active token's room.
Move the named suspect and weapon pieces into that room.
Check opponents in turn order beginning immediately after the active player.
For each opponent, calculate matching cards.
If no match exists, record a pass and continue.
If one or more matches exist, require that player to choose exactly one.
Reveal the chosen card only to the suggester unless a special card says otherwise.
If all opponents pass, record the unanswered suggestion state.
Apply the edition's accusation timing rule.
accusation_resolution_algorithm: Validate that the investigator is eligible to accuse under the selected rules profile.
Validate that the investigator has not already made a strict final accusation.
Validate any configured room or location requirement.
Accept exactly one suspect, one weapon, and one room.
Compare all three IDs against the server-only solution.
If all three match, resolve victory according to the selected playstyle.
If any differ, apply the selected incorrect-accusation consequence without revealing the solution.
Keep the incorrect accuser's evidence hand available for future ordered disproval when strict classic consequences are enabled.
If no eligible investigator can still win, resolve the configured unsolved ending.

two_human_player_handling.default_for_this_game: No special two-player set-aside system is required because two humans are automatically joined by four adventurer bots, creating six investigative seats.

optional_pure_two_side_variant.why_special_rules_are_needed: With only two investigative sides, ordinary card revelation produces less varied information and can make deduction too direct. Special setups hide extra non-solution cards outside both hands.

circa_2011_hasbro_method.setup: After creating the solution, place four remaining deduction cards face down in a row beside the board before dealing.
circa_2011_hasbro_method.information_rule: When the other player or team cannot answer a suggestion, the active side secretly examines one of the four set-aside cards, using a different card on later unanswered suggestions.
circa_2011_hasbro_method.bonus_cards: Red Bonus cards are not used in this two-player/team mode.

2023_refresh_method.setup: After creating the solution, place four remaining deduction cards face down in four rooms, then deal the rest.
2023_refresh_method.information_rule: When a player enters a room containing one of these cards, the player privately examines it, marks it off, and returns it face down.

optional_pure_two_side_variant.team_guidance: A team should act as one investigative side under the chosen edition's rules. Teams should agree in advance whether notes and private reveals may be discussed openly within the team.

room_theory_algorithm: Verify the accuser is a living non-killer and physically occupies a solution-eligible room.
Set the accused room to the accuser’s current room; the UI cannot name a different room.
Accept one suspected original-killer Character card and one murder-evidence Weapon card.
Block any Character, Weapon, or Room card currently in the accuser’s own evidence hand; an accusation is based on cards the accuser does not have.
Ask every living evidence holder, including bots, to play all named cards they hold. Each played card turns face-up publicly and proves that category choice is not in the envelope.
The original killer has no evidence hand and therefore cannot play a disproof card.
If no living hand plays a card, check the shuffled Gameplay Keep deck containing evidence returned by dead characters.
Reveal every matching Keep-deck card and mark it public; the accusation is disproved if any match exists.
If no living hand and no Keep-deck card can disprove the exact three-card combination, offer the eligible accuser the choice to continue investigating or lock it in as the Final Accusation.
Record all played cards on the public case board and every legal private inference in the accuser’s notebook.
privacy: The sealed solution stays server-only until a correct Final Accusation or post-match reveal.
Starting evidence hands are private to living non-killer seats.
Legally played disproof cards become public face-up evidence.
Ghosts have no evidence hand and cannot accuse, report, vote, or communicate unrestricted solution information.
The opening victim does not learn the killer merely by entering Ghost Mode.

location_requirement.room_theory: A living, conscious character must physically occupy a legal cell in the named room.
location_requirement.final_accusation: A living, conscious character must physically occupy a legal cell in the accused room.
location_requirement.library: Either Library floor area satisfies the Library location requirement.
location_requirement.not_rooms: Hallways, stairs, service passages, landings, and secret-passage transit cells cannot host a theory or accusation.

not_holding_requirement.rule: The accuser may name only a Character, evidence Weapon, and occupied Room card that are absent from the accuser’s own hand.
not_holding_requirement.client_validation: Disable any card the player holds and reject tampered requests server-side.
not_holding_requirement.reasoning: A player’s own cards already prove those elements are not in the envelope.

room_theory_sequence: A living, conscious character physically enters a solution room and chooses Room Theory.
The current room is filled automatically. The theorist names one Character and one evidence Weapon that are absent from their own hand.
The server validates occupancy, hand restrictions, living status, and unresolved encounter state.
In deterministic seat order, every living human or bot—including the original killer—who holds one or more named cards must play every matching card face-up into the public Disproof Zone.
The server also checks the protected Keep deck for matching cards returned by later dead characters and plays every match.
After the reveal window, played cards return to the correct private hand or protected Keep deck; the public case board records each disproved element.
If no card is played, mark an Unrefuted Lead and offer the theorist the option to escalate to a Final Accusation if otherwise eligible.
murder_mystery_system.bot_behavior: Bots, including a killer bot, maintain private five-card evidence hands, refuse theories containing their own cards, and automatically play every required matching card.
murder_mystery_system.ghost_rule: Ghosts cannot make theories, play living evidence cards, or accuse.

killer_evidence_rule.server_enforcement: A matching killer card is auto-committed to the Disproof Zone under the same timing and animation as every other matching card.
killer_evidence_rule.privacy: The reveal identifies the card owner seat, not that seat’s secret role.
killer_evidence_rule.final_accusation: The original killer cannot make a Final Accusation.

source_resolution_notes: The detailed Characters document identifies Jock as Lizardfolk, while the compact gameplay roster uses Gecko. This concept uses Lizardfolk and stores Gecko as a legacy label.
One card document mentions fifteen room cards, while the complete gameplay rules name sixteen rooms and separately state sixteen room cards. This concept uses the complete sixteen-room list.

Original power names are retained as design references. Their final game text and balance should be rewritten against the chosen licensed D&D SRD or replaced with original equivalent wording before publication.
The canonical human player range is 2-8, overriding source concepts that proposed 1-8, 3-8, 4-12, or other ranges.
Matches with two to five humans are automatically filled to six adventurers with unique bot-controlled heroes.
In Work Together, adventurer bots are allies; in Work Separately, adventurer bots are rivals.
Schema 4.0.0 supersedes the older passive-culprit rule: every match has one active human or bot killer, and that controller is privately told at match start.
Schema 4.0.0 makes body reports, meetings, killer sabotage, and the active hidden killer core systems while preserving the required three-part suspect/weapon/room accusation.
The complete sixteen-room list is canonical where one older source stated fifteen rooms.
The canonical eight named heroes replace generic placeholder class entries from the mobile design source.
Generated placeholder catalogs such as Evidence Type 1, NPC 1, Task 1, and Achievement 1 are preserved only in the noncanonical source archive and are not treated as finished game content.
NumPad 1 and NumPad 7 remain reserved and cannot activate flying, climbing, swimming, hovering, levitation, or vertical movement.
Exploration movement uses a server-authoritative roll, legal endpoint highlights, destination selection, path preview, and synchronized token movement; D&D combat uses speed-based tactical movement.
Full PvP violence never changes the sealed main-killer identity; the original murderer remains the one character in the envelope.
The focused D&D JSON pack supplies the runtime combat actions, weapons, conditions, monsters, traps, and usable item records merged into canonical runtime catalogs.

assignment_rules: Human players choose heroes first unless the host enables random assignment.

Bot takeover preserves the disconnected seat’s killer or non-killer role.

dungeon_director_rules.identity: Autonomous Dungeon Master combat-and-hazard controller for exported Belavadös 5e mini-games.
dungeon_director_rules.dm_not_replaced: The human DM still designs the encounter, reviews balance, and controls table consent. During the mini-game, the bot can run hostiles and hazards so the DM does not need to micromanage them.
decision_loop: Read current room states, objective progress, initiative order, HP, conditions, visibility, sound, and threat levels.
Update timers: traps, locked doors, reinforcements, lair actions, recharge, hazards, and objectives.
For each hostile on initiative, choose the legal action with the highest tactical score.
Resolve movement path, line of sight, cover, attacks, saves, damage, and conditions.
Narrate the result briefly, then hand control back to the next player or bot unit.
fairness_rules: The bot cannot use information the hostile could not plausibly know unless the hostile has special senses, telepathy, scouting, or room sensors.
The bot should respect action economy, movement, line of sight, cooldowns, recharge, and conditions.
A trap should give at least one detection or counterplay path unless it is intentionally brutal and labeled by the DM.
The bot should not chain unavoidable failures; after a major failure, offer a response window.
The bot can play enemies intelligently, but it should preserve fun, pacing, and clear feedback.

fairness_rules: The killer cannot edit the envelope, evidence-card ownership, server dice, movement reachability, item instances, or combat logs.
Planted clues are always classified internally as physical clues, never absolute evidence cards.
Killer actions require legal range, line of sight, cooldown, action cost, and server validation.
A killer may be attacked by monsters, harmed by traps, downed, looted, or killed under the same D&D rules unless a power says otherwise.
The killer cannot use full-solution knowledge to make a winning investigator accusation.
Bots never read hidden role state belonging to another seat.

board_cell_contract.clickable_rule: Every rendered board square has a hit target, keyboard focus target, controller focus target, and accessible label.
board_cell_contract.walkability: A cell may be visible and clickable for inspection while still being illegal as a movement endpoint.
board_cell_contract.floor_changes: Only through stairs, ladders, elevators, teleporters, drops, or passages explicitly linked in the map graph.

turn_state_machine.server_action: generate and broadcast signed roll result
run weighted reachability from current token cell using movement budget and current hidden/public blockers
revalidate board revision, path, occupancy, door state, hazards, and movement cost
reserve destination and broadcast authoritative path animation
resolve opportunity attacks, entered-square traps, discoveries, doors, room entry, passage prompts, and encounter triggers in path order

reachability.algorithm: weighted breadth-first search or Dijkstra over the authoritative board graph
reachability.doors: open doors cost normal movement; closed unlocked doors may be opened as a free interaction if available; locked or barred doors block pathing
reachability.rooms: entering a solution room through a legal doorway is a valid endpoint and ends exploration movement by default
reachability.traps: undiscovered traps do not reveal themselves during highlight calculation; entering their trigger cell resolves them after movement reaches that cell
reachability.secret_passages: only discovered/unlocked passage edges appear for ordinary players; every player may use them once available
reachability.hidden_information: client receives only legal endpoint IDs and permitted path previews, never hidden blocker or trap metadata
reachability.cross_floor_edges: Normal stairs and discovered two-way secret passages are graph edges with configured movement cost; undiscovered secret passages are private/absent from the player graph.

highlight_and_selection.reachable_endpoints: Highlight every legal end cell whose minimum path cost is less than or equal to the movement budget.
highlight_and_selection.path_preview: Hover, focus, or touch-and-hold a highlighted endpoint to preview the chosen shortest legal path, movement cost, room entry, and known hazards.
highlight_and_selection.multiple_paths: When equal-cost paths exist, the player may cycle paths before confirming.
highlight_and_selection.nonreachable_cells: Remain clickable for inspection but cannot be selected as an end destination.
accessibility: screen-reader announcement of distance and blockers

selection_inputs.keyboard: focus highlighted cell and press Enter/Space
selection_inputs.controller: focus highlighted cell and press confirm button

highlight_and_selection.confirmation: Single confirm by default; optional second confirmation for dangerous known trap or hostile endpoint.
highlight_and_selection.svg_contract: Every SVG contains 1,536 interactive rect.map-cell elements and exposes window.KeepMap methods for highlight, clear, select, and inspect.

token_animation.speed: configurable, with instant and reduced-motion options
token_animation.step_events: Each entered cell is resolved in sequence; animation pauses when an encounter, trap, body report, reaction, or forced stop occurs.
token_animation.final_commit: Token logical position updates on the server and all clients receive the same revision number.
token_animation.rejection_behavior: If revalidation fails because the board changed, do not move; recalculate and re-highlight from the current cell.

secret_passage_runtime.usable_by: every living player and adventurer bot
secret_passage_runtime.discovery: Perception, Investigation, magic, room clue, lever, movable statue, map item, or witnessing another user
secret_passage_runtime.activation: Select the passage interaction while in its entrance cell or room entry zone.
secret_passage_runtime.movement_cost: ends the current exploration movement and moves to the linked exit unless a power says otherwise
secret_passage_runtime.exit_validation: exit must exist; occupied exits use the nearest legal linked exit cell or queue the passage
secret_passage_runtime.killer_rule: killer may know additional passage entrances at start, but use can leave tracks, residue, sound, or witness evidence
secret_passage_runtime.encounter_chance: passage use may trigger a configured monster, trap, or clue event

acceptance_tests: After a valid roll, at least the current square and every legal endpoint within budget are returned; no endpoint over budget is returned.
Selecting a non-highlighted cell never moves the token.
Selecting a highlighted cell moves the token along a legal path and synchronizes the same final cell to every client.
Locked doors, occupied enemy cells, blocked terrain, and undiscovered passage edges are respected.
Entering a trap cell can interrupt movement and resolve the trap before the remaining path.
Entering a monster threat zone can transition to initiative.
A stale client board revision causes rejection and recalculation rather than desynchronization.
Mouse, touch, keyboard, and controller can all roll, inspect, select, and confirm destinations.
Each of four floors loads a 48×32 grid with exactly 1,536 clickable cells.
Cross-floor movement changes floor_id atomically and never leaves a token on two floors.
Room names are not visibly rendered on SVG maps.

conditions.effect: Cannot see; attacks against the creature have Advantage, and its attacks have Disadvantage. Automatically fails sight-dependent checks.

conditions.effect: Cannot attack or directly harm the charmer and the charmer has Advantage on social checks against it. Does not force evidence revelation or accusation choices.

conditions.effect: Cannot hear and automatically fails hearing-dependent checks.

conditions.name: Frightened
conditions.effect: Has Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks while the fear source is visible and cannot willingly move closer to it.

conditions.name: Grappled
conditions.effect: Speed becomes 0. Ends if the grappler is incapacitated or the creature escapes.

conditions.name: Incapacitated
conditions.effect: Cannot take Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions and loses Concentration.

conditions.name: Invisible
conditions.effect: Cannot be seen without a special sense; attacks against it have Disadvantage and its attacks have Advantage when location is known.

conditions.effect: Incapacitated, speed 0, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks from within 5 feet that hit are critical hits.

conditions.name: Poisoned
conditions.effect: Has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

conditions.effect: Crawls at extra movement cost; attacks within 5 feet have Advantage, farther attacks have Disadvantage; its attacks have Disadvantage.

conditions.name: Restrained

trap_runtime.presentation: Undiscovered traps have no identifying highlight. Discovered traps gain an accessible marker, threat radius, known trigger, and interaction menu.
trap_runtime.disarm: Choose a legal skill, tool, spell, environmental action, brute-force action, rescue, or deliberate trigger; roll against the trap record.
trap_runtime.trigger: Resolve in entered-square order, pause movement when required, apply save/attack, damage, condition, forced movement, room lock, timer, or spawn.
trap_runtime.killer_use: Killer sabotage may rearm or redirect compatible traps but cannot skip cooldown, range, access, or server validation.
trap_runtime.pvp_use: In Full PvP, any character may lure or shove another character into an armed trap through legal D&D actions.

container_and_treasure_runtime.loot_presentation: Treasure appears as world pickups, container slots, defeated-enemy drops, objective rewards, or evidence rewards with name, icon key, category, effect, activation, quantity/charges, value, and ownership.
container_and_treasure_runtime.equipment: Worn and held items can be equipped to compatible slots and immediately alter derived actions or stats.
container_and_treasure_runtime.trade: Direct offer/accept trade in both modes; Full PvP may also permit theft, pickpocketing, corpse looting, and dropped-item races.
container_and_treasure_runtime.ownership_history: Every unique item instance records spawn source, prior owners, transfers, drops, thefts, uses, and destruction.
container_and_treasure_runtime.quick_slots: Players may assign usable items and powers to keyboard, touch, or controller quick slots.
container_and_treasure_runtime.scoring: Configured treasure value contributes to secondary placement without preventing item use.

player_pvp_runtime.work_together: Server rejects intentional non-killer attacks against non-killers. Killer attacks, monster attacks, environmental damage, and allowed controlled effects remain legal.
player_pvp_runtime.full_pvp: Every living player and bot may target any other legal creature with D&D attacks, powers, shoves, grapples, theft, traps, or environmental actions.
player_pvp_runtime.downed_and_death: At 0 HP use Downed/death-save rules. Confirmed death enters Ghost Mode. A legal revival within two rounds restores living play; otherwise the ghost remains a non-participating spectator until match end.
player_pvp_runtime.body_creation: A dead or permanently eliminated hero leaves a reportable body/evidence marker and configured loot access.
player_pvp_runtime.main_killer_identity: PvP kill credit never changes the sealed main killer.
player_pvp_runtime.ghost_collision: Ghosts phase through walls, doors, floors, creatures, traps, and terrain and never reserve or block a square.

movement: A player cannot move before rolling in exploration.
The roll result produces a finite set of server-calculated legal highlighted endpoints.
Clicking/tapping/focusing a highlighted endpoint previews and then commits a legal path.
The token visibly traverses the board and every client ends with the same authoritative cell.
Doors, floors, terrain, occupancy, secret passages, traps, reactions, and room entry are resolved correctly.
hidden_killer: Exactly one active seat receives the killer role in every match.
The killer seat exactly matches the suspect in the sealed envelope.
The killer receives a private role reveal; non-killers do not receive the solution.
A human or bot can be killer, and reconnect/bot takeover preserves the role.
The killer cannot submit the known solution for an investigator victory.
clue_deduction: Exactly one suspect, weapon, and room are sealed and immutable.
Room theories use ordered private disproval.
Evidence cards, public clues, physical clues, and planted clues remain distinguishable by the server.
A correct three-part accusation ends or ranks the match according to mode.
An incorrect accusation never leaks the envelope.
dnd_gameplay: Monsters spawn as targetable tokens with AC, HP, speed, attacks, traits, initiative, AI, and defeat rewards.
Traps can be detected, marked, disarmed, bypassed, triggered, resolved, rescued from, and sometimes rearmed.
Treasure and items can be found, inspected, picked up, used, equipped, dropped, traded, and scored where allowed.
PvP and monster combat resolve attacks, saves, damage, conditions, healing, death saves, bodies, and revival.
Secret passages are usable by all players and bots once discovered or unlocked.
mode_rules: Work Together blocks intentional innocent-on-innocent damage while permitting killer attacks and hostile encounters.
Full PvP permits attacks among all adventurers without changing who the main killer is.
The killer has separate victory rules in both modes.
Reports and meetings work in both modes and do not replace the final Clue accusation.
A confirmed-dead player enters Ghost Mode and can see every player and traverse walls and floors.
Ghosts cannot report, call meetings, vote, accuse, communicate clues to living players, interact, block movement, or affect victory.
A valid revival within the two-round window removes Ghost Mode and returns the player to authoritative living play.
cross_platform: Mouse, touch, keyboard, arrow keys, NumPad, Xbox-compatible, Nintendo-compatible, and PlayStation-compatible inputs can complete the full roll-to-move flow.

haunting_actions.effect: Set off an already armed built-in or Trap-deck trap when a legal trigger exists.
Draw the top Trap card and place it on a server-approved tile in the current or adjacent connected room.
Raise or lower a monster's interest in a legal room, noise source, scent trail, patrol point, or target category.
Request one legal monster movement toward an adjacent square or connected room during the next monster phase.
Close, bar, rattle, or briefly lock one hauntable door with an available counterplay.
Alter one room's lighting for a short duration.
Move or animate a hauntable prop to create noise, distraction, cover, or a visual cue without fabricating evidence.
Create a directional warning, false trail, intimidation cue, or atmospheric effect.
Reveal a trap outline briefly, distract a monster, or extend a rescue window without revealing private cards.
Temporarily control an authored armor suit, statue, chandelier, bell, mirror, or ritual anchor.

vote, break ties, or count toward quorum

draw or hold normal Gameplay evidence

death_card_recycle.title: Card Return, Shuffle, and Ghost Transition on Permanent Death
return_to_source_decks: Every evidence card in the deceased living character’s hand returns to the Evidence deck.
Every unconsumed deck-owned Treasure card carried, equipped, attuned, reserved, or held by the deceased returns to the Treasure deck.
Every Armory Weapon card owned by the deceased returns to the Armory Weapon deck unless a card was permanently consumed by a legal upgrade effect.
Every held Trap, Monster-control, summon, or other shared-deck card returns to its own source deck.
Any cards mistakenly predealt to the off-screen opening victim return before active play.
resolution_order: confirm permanent death or opening-victim assignment
freeze hand, inventory, equipment, attunement, and pending card effects
group eligible cards by source deck
remove ownership and expire temporary ownership effects
return each card to its source draw deck
shuffle every affected deck with authoritative randomness
create or continue the character’s ghost state
death_card_recycle.server_authority: Only the authoritative match runtime may return and shuffle cards.
death_card_recycle.revival_rule: Cards already returned and shuffled are not recreated if the character is later revived; the revived character resumes with no duplicate cards.

public_gameplay_card_policy.loot_and_encounter_cards: Weapon, Treasure, Trap, and Monster details become visible only when their card is legally drawn, revealed, or activated.

setup_sequence: Select one original-killer Character card, one evidence Weapon card, and one Room card for the server-only envelope.
Select a different active character as the opening victim.
Privately brief the killer with role, victim, murder room, murder weapon, cover objectives, and killer victory condition.
Place the victim body in the murder room and transition that seat directly to Ghost Mode.
Shuffle the remaining 35 evidence cards and deal exactly 5 cards to each of the 7 living players/bots, including the killer.
Privately show each living seat its five-card hand. No UI or network payload identifies which hand belongs to the killer.
Place living tokens at the mode-specific starter cells, subject only to a safe opening-body conflict adjustment.
Instantiate authored locks, fixed traps, hidden monsters, containers, searchable fixtures, and configured random traps.

original_killer.combat_rule: The opening murder may be cinematic. Every later attempted murder uses the ordinary D&D-style combat, damage, downed, rescue, and death systems.
original_killer.if_killed: Becomes an original-killer ghost and continues hostile haunting, but cannot make living-character attacks or living accusations.

secondary_killers.creation: Intentional permanent playable-character kill by a non-original-killer.
secondary_killers.knowledge: A secondary killer is privately told their new status and objective.
secondary_killers.case_integrity: Later murders are recorded separately; the opening solution envelope never changes.

resolve a character or room reward
treasure_deck.screen_behavior: The card appears and can be kept, equipped, traded, consumed, or returned according to its rules.
treasure_deck.permanent_death: All held deck-owned Treasure cards return to the Treasure deck and shuffle.
treasure_deck.mundane_weapon_separation: Ordinary nonmagical weapons are drawn from the Armory Weapon deck, not the Treasure deck.
treasure_deck.magic_weapon_separation: Magic weapons are Weapon-deck cards, not Treasure-deck cards, unless an authored quest explicitly awards a named weapon card.

monster_deck.contents: Keep-appropriate monster encounter cards with current/max HP data.
monster_deck.screen_behavior: Reveal the monster card, spawn it on the nearest legal square, show an HP bar, and enter initiative when hostile.
monster_deck.resolution: Affected living characters enter initiative. The monster can be defeated, escaped, contained, befriended if allowed, or left persistent in the room.
monster_deck.ghost_interaction: Ghosts may influence legal movement, patrol destination, room interest, or aggression cues but cannot make illegal attacks.
monster_deck.permanent_death: Held summon or control cards return to the Monster deck. Independent active monsters remain until their encounter resolves.
monster_deck.automatic_authored_spawns: All nine mapped monster instances exist at match setup, hidden at their authored cells.

trap_deck.purpose: Represent fixed trap cards referenced by the map and random temporary traps.
draw_triggers: interact with an authored trapped door, passage, chest, or bookshelf
trap_deck.screen_behavior: The card pops up, places a legal temporary hazard, displays counters, and starts a synchronized countdown.
trap_deck.disarm: Use a D&D-style Search and tool sequence: detect with Passive Perception or a Search action using Wisdom (Perception), study mechanisms with Intelligence (Investigation) when useful, and disarm a mechanical trap with a Dexterity check using Thieves’ Tools against the trap disable DC. Tool proficiency adds Proficiency Bonus; matching skill proficiency grants Advantage under the revised tool rule. Magical traps may instead allow Intelligence (Arcana), Dispel Magic, a listed spell, or a card-specific counter.
trap_deck.success: Disable the trap, gain XP, and receive configured Treasure or Gameplay rewards.
trap_deck.failure: Apply damage, conditions, alarm, separation, lockdown, monster draw, or environmental effects.
trap_deck.ghost_interaction: Every ghost can trigger an armed trap or spend Haunt Energy to draw and place a new legal Trap card.
trap_deck.fairness: No random trap may spawn on a protected starting cell, meeting zone, inaccessible tile, or unavoidable no-counterplay route.
trap_deck.permanent_death: Unused held Trap cards return to the Trap deck. Resolved cards enter discard and reshuffle when needed.

monster_trigger_cards.rule: Some Trap cards do not deal their main effect directly. They instruct the active seat to draw a Monster card, spawn that monster on a valid adjacent or room spawn cell, show its HP bar, and begin initiative.

trap_deck.monster_ambush: Instead of placing a normal hazard, draw the top Monster card and spawn that monster on the nearest legal unoccupied cell.
trap_deck.detection_and_disarm: Use the D&D interaction procedure defined in dnd_video_game_engine.search_locks_and_traps.

applies_to: failed death saves or other permanent death
atomic_sequence: return every deck-owned card to its matching source deck
global_card_return_on_permanent_death.solution_protection: Envelope cards never move, redraw, replace, or return.
global_card_return_on_permanent_death.opening_victim_exception: The opening victim dies before evidence is dealt and therefore returns no starting hand.

weapon_deck.contents: Thirty-six keep-appropriate revised-rules weapons: all non-firearm Simple and Martial weapons from the referenced 2024 Basic Rules table.
draw_triggers: open a weapon-bearing chest or hidden weapon cache
resolve a Trap or Monster card that awards a weapon draw
use a room or character ability that explicitly finds a physical weapon
weapon_rack_sequence: Move adjacent to or onto the weapon-rack interaction cell.
Use the Search or Investigate interaction.
Resolve any authored monster trigger or hidden trap attached to the rack.
Draw exactly one Weapon card from the authoritative Weapon deck.
Reveal the physical weapon to the drawing seat and add it to inventory.
Mark that rack spent unless a rule explicitly refreshes it.

proficiency_and_use.rule: Anyone may attempt to wield a weapon, but only a proficient character adds Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls.
proficiency_and_use.game_classification: A weapon is class-compatible when the character is proficient through class or an explicit character override.
proficiency_and_use.unusable_item_definition: A found Weapon-deck item for which the character lacks proficiency or cannot satisfy a required property such as Heavy ability minimum.
proficiency_and_use.mastery: Mastery activates only when the character has a feature that unlocks that mastery for the weapon.

unusable_weapon_hoarding_penalty.applies_to: Weapon-deck cards carried but not class-compatible/effectively usable by the carrier.
does_not_apply_to: ordinary Treasure cards unless another encumbrance rule applies
ends_when: store it in a legal container
trade it to another living character
gain proficiency that makes it usable

trade_requirements: same room or adjacent legal squares
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.transfer: The physical Weapon card moves from donor inventory to recipient inventory.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.receiver_bonus: When the recipient is proficient with the traded weapon, the recipient upgrades their own currently equipped signature weapon to +1.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.plus_one_effect: +1 to attack rolls and +1 to damage rolls made with the upgraded weapon.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.recipient_choice: The recipient may instead designate the newly received weapon as their own equipped weapon and apply the +1 to it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.non_stacking: A character’s trade upgrade stops at +1. Further trades do not produce +2 or higher unless a separate explicit rule grants it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.anti_loop: Each physical Weapon card can trigger this trade upgrade once per match, and trading the same card back and forth never retriggers it.
trade_and_plus_one_upgrade.movement_update: The donor’s hoarding penalty recalculates immediately after the weapon leaves their inventory.

weapon_deck.death_return: All held Weapon-deck cards return face down to the Weapon deck and the deck is shuffled before control transfers fully to Ghost Mode.

evidence_deck.solution_setup: Seal one Character, one evidence Weapon, and one Room card server-side.
evidence_deck.starting_deal: After sealing three solution cards and selecting the separate opening victim, deal all 35 remaining evidence cards as seven private five-card hands. Every living seat—including the killer—receives one hand. The opening-victim ghost receives none.
evidence_deck.private_hands: Only the owning authenticated seat and server-authoritative bot logic can see a hand.
evidence_deck.physical_room_disproof: During a legal room theory, every living player/bot holding any named card plays every matching card face-up into the temporary Disproof Zone. Cards return to their owners after all living players see them.
evidence_deck.keep_deck_after_death: Evidence cards held by a later permanently dead character return face down to the protected Keep deck. During a legal theory, the server also plays every matching Keep-deck card to the Disproof Zone, then reshuffles it.
evidence_deck.opening_victim_hand: The opening victim receives no cards because the victim is dead before the 35-card deal.
evidence_deck.card_face_restriction: Evidence cards identify only their character, evidence weapon, or room and may not mention traps, locks, secret passages, searchable fixtures, hidden items, monster spawns, or treasure.
evidence_deck.killer_hand_rule: The killer hand is indistinguishable in size, card backs, network schema, and UI from every other living hand. The killer must publicly play all matching cards during disproof.
evidence_deck.room_theory: Any living, conscious character, including the killer for cover, may make a legal room theory from the room they physically occupy. The theorist may not name cards in their own hand.
evidence_deck.final_accusation_killer_restriction: The original killer cannot submit or win through a Final Accusation because they were given the solution at setup.

armory_weapon_deck.source_basis: Mundane weapon statistics use SRD 5.2.1. Magic inserts use SRD 5.2.1 magic items and retain their named extra energy/damage types.
armory_weapon_deck.official_rule_note: Official D&D permits anyone to wield a weapon but withholds the Proficiency Bonus when the wielder lacks proficiency.
armory_weapon_deck.killer_in_the_keep_override: For this game, a character who is not compatible with a found weapon cannot equip or attack with it; they may carry or trade it.
armory_weapon_deck.draw_rule: Investigate a weapon rack and resolve its Search/encounter trigger, then draw and reveal exactly one top card from this deck. Determine compatibility only after the card is revealed.

carry_penalty.applies_to: Each carried Armory Weapon card the carrier cannot use.
carry_penalty.legacy_roll_movement: Subtract 1 traversable grid square from the movement die result per incompatible carried weapon; minimum final result 0 squares.
carry_penalty.tactical_speed_equivalent: Subtract 5 feet of movement per incompatible carried weapon for the turn; minimum 0 feet after all modifiers.
carry_penalty.equipped_or_compatible_cards: No penalty from compatible weapons, equipped weapons, evidence Weapon cards, or non-weapon treasure.

requirements: Both characters are living and conscious.
Both occupy the same named room or adjacent legal grid cells.
Recipient is compatible with the traded weapon.
Trade is accepted by the recipient or their bot logic.
trade_rule.enhancement: The recipient immediately gives their currently equipped weapon a permanent +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls for the remainder of the match.
trade_rule.stacking: Bonuses can stack to a maximum of +3 on one equipped weapon.
trade_rule.anti_exploit: Each Armory Weapon card can grant this enhancement only once. After granting it, mark the card bound_to_upgrade and remove it from further trade loops until match end.
trade_rule.unequipped_recipient: If the recipient has no equipped weapon, they equip the received weapon and it becomes +1.
